hyps.why: With edge 0 removed node 1 gets no input, so a conv on edge 4 is dead and adds nothing.
Edge 2 carries no signal when node 1 is disconnected from the input, so the edit has no effect.
Replacing a removed direct input-to-output edge with a conv adds a whole new path, a bigger gain than replacing an existing op.
Adding a skip path where there was none improves gradient flow far more than swapping another op for a skip.
Restoring the final edge from node 2 into the output from nothing gives a large gain.
Connecting node 1 to the input activates the edge 2 and edge 4 branches, so the gain is large.
Replacing none with a conv enables a new input-to-node-2 path, which is worth more than replacing an existing op.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, the edge 5 conv is a more critical route to the output, so it adds more.
Replacing a pooling op, which still passes some useful signal, gains less than filling an empty edge, so the gain is smaller than when the edge is none.
Edge 4 is unreachable from the input when edge 0 is none, so the edit has no effect.
